scenes.say: Imagine this. Two installers quote your house, with two very different panel counts.
The answer is already on your electric bill.
The average US home uses about ten thousand eight hundred kilowatt-hours a year.
That works out to roughly seventeen to twenty-five panels of four hundred to four hundred fifty watts.
But your local sunshine changes the answer by thirty percent or more. The same home needs fewer panels in Arizona than in Washington.
Want to size your own system? Read the free guide at viva voltia dot com.
